name: t1.7-nursing-workforce
title: Published global nursing Gini cannot be checked from the paper

sources.title: Kharazmi, Bordbar and Bordbar, Distribution of nursing workforce in the world using Gini coefficient, BMC Nursing 22:151 (2023)

moveq.original: The global Gini of the nursing workforce is 0.667.
moveq.moveq_question: Can 0.667 be independently verified from the paper?
blocked_reasons: The stated formula is Gini = 1 − Σ(Xi × Yi), with Xi and Yi as cumulative percentages of population and nurses. That is not the trapezoid Lorenz form used by moveq, and it is incomplete as written.
Table 1 publishes HDI-group aggregates only (four rows). There is no country-by-country table for the 189 countries, so the headline 0.667 cannot be rebuilt from the article.
Data availability is 'from the corresponding author on reasonable request', not a deposited per-country file.
Country-equal versus population weighting is undisclosed; either convention is defensible and they are not the same number.
limitations: This case documents why the published 0.667 cannot be checked. It does not estimate a substitute Gini.
The four HDI-group rows are the between-group table (published 0.467), not the 189-country series.
A WHO NHWA and UN rebuild would be a separate RECOMPUTED case, never a reproduction of 0.667.
The measure, were it computable, would still be descriptive, not causal.
